fine_trace.note: Attacker-controlled template bytes are copied into a 32768-byte static buffer and NUL-terminated.
The template string is compiled with the CONST_TEMPLATE flag, so text chunks reference the static copy buffer directly.
Short text runs (<= 8 bytes) are packed into the chunk data pointer as ACTION_APPEND_SMALL chunks.

fine_trace.code: struct lwan_strbuf *buf = lwan_strbuf_from_lexeme(parser, lexeme); emit_chunk(parser, ACTION_APPEND, 0, buf);
fine_trace.note: Longer text runs create a static lwan_strbuf pointing into the fuzzer's copy buffer (CONST_TEMPLATE).
A variable reference emits an ACTION_VARIABLE chunk holding the descriptor pointer.
An iteration start emits an ACTION_START_ITER chunk with FLAGS_NO_FREE set.
The matching end emits ACTION_END_ITER whose data is the index of the start chunk.
At EOF an ACTION_LAST sentinel chunk is appended.

fine_trace.code: for (prev_chunk = chunk;; chunk++) { if (chunk->action == ACTION_LAST) { ... return false; } if (chunk->action == ACTION_END_ITER) { ... if (prev_index == start_index) { ... break; } } }
fine_trace.note: For each ACTION_START_ITER the loop scans forward for the matching ACTION_END_ITER; if the end chunk's stored start index does not equal the current start's index, the loop keeps incrementing chunk past the array bounds.
When a match is found, the end chunk's data is replaced with a pointer to the start chunk, and the start chunk's data is replaced with a malloc'd chunk_descriptor.
The compiled template is freed; ACTION_APPEND chunks free their static strbufs, and ACTION_START_ITER/ACTION_IF chunks free their chunk_descriptor.

fine_trace.code: if (chunk->flags & FLAGS_NO_FREE) return; switch (chunk->action) { ... case ACTION_APPEND: lwan_strbuf_free(chunk->data); break; ... }
fine_trace.note: A chunk whose flags were corrupted or whose data was overwritten can cause a write to freed or out-of-bounds memory during teardown, producing the global-buffer-overflow WRITE.
